slides.title: Quadratic Equations
slides.speaker_notes: Welcome students. From linear (degree 1) we move up to quadratic (degree 2).

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Solve by factorisation, completing the square, and the formula.
Use the discriminant to predict the nature of roots.
slides.speaker_notes: Read each objective; ask which feels least sure.

slides.title: Standard form
bullets: If a = 0, equation collapses to linear.
Always re-arrange before applying any method.
Coefficients a, b, c are read directly from the standard form.
slides.speaker_notes: Demonstrate re-arranging (x − 2)^2 = 5 → x^2 − 4x − 1 = 0 on the board.

slides.title: Roots — verification by substitution
bullets: A root is a value of x making LHS = 0.
A quadratic has AT MOST TWO real roots.
Number of real roots is determined by the discriminant.
slides.speaker_notes: Substitute and check is the simplest verification — drill it.

slides.title: Method 1 — Factorisation
bullets: Apply the zero-product property: P · Q = 0 → P = 0 or Q = 0.
Set each factor to 0 and solve.
Limitation: only works when factors are rational.
slides.speaker_notes: The zero-product property is the why behind factor-and-solve.

slides.title: Factor: 2x^2 − 7x + 3 = 0
slides.speaker_notes: Split the middle, regroup, apply zero-product.

slides.title: Method 2 — Completing the square
bullets: 1. Divide by a so leading coefficient is 1.
4. Re-write LHS as (x + b/(2a))^2 ; take square roots.
slides.speaker_notes: Walk through carefully — this is also where the quadratic formula comes from.

slides.title: Complete the square: x^2 − 6x + 5 = 0
slides.speaker_notes: Pause at the (x − 3)^2 = 4 step — that's the elegant insight.

slides.title: Method 3 — The quadratic formula
bullets: Universal solver — works for ANY quadratic.
Derived by completing the square on the general form.
Steps: identify a, b, c; compute discriminant; substitute.
slides.speaker_notes: Memorise the formula; emphasis on its universality.

slides.title: Discriminant — nature of roots
bullets: Geometric: parabola crosses, touches, or misses the x-axis.
slides.speaker_notes: Sketch the three parabola pictures on the board.

slides.title: Discriminant cases
bullets: x^2 + x + 1 = 0: D = −3 < 0 → no real roots.
slides.speaker_notes: Three small computations; students see the pattern instantly.

slides.title: Roots and coefficients
bullets: If α, β are roots of ax^2 + bx + c = 0:
Build a quadratic from given roots: x^2 − (sum)x + (product) = 0.
slides.speaker_notes: Useful in reverse: given roots, write down the quadratic instantly.

slides.title: Word problem: rectangle area
bullets: Length is 4 m more than width; area is 192 m².

slides.title: You try (5 minutes)
bullets: 2. Solve x^2 + 4x − 5 = 0 by completing the square.
3. Use the formula on x^2 − x − 1 = 0.
slides.speaker_notes: Walk the room; address common slips.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q2. D < 0 means how many real roots?
slides.speaker_notes: Address the question with the most disagreement.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Quadratic = degree 2; ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.
Solve by factorisation / completing the square / quadratic formula.
Discriminant D = b^2 − 4ac → nature of roots.
Word problems: set up, solve, REJECT non-physical roots.
slides.speaker_notes: Hand out the worksheet, announce homework.
